gloss: speaking of which; come to think of it; that reminds me

definitions.gloss: speaking of which; come to think of it; that reminds me
definitions.explanation: A conversational connector used to introduce a topic that the speaker has just been reminded of, usually by something the other person said. Marks a slight shift to a related point.

examples.japanese: そういえば、⟦{昨日|きのう}→昨日：00859_kinou⟧⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{会|あ}った→会う：00482_au⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: Come to think of it, I ran into him yesterday.

examples.japanese: そういえば、⟦{宿題|しゅくだい}→宿題：00812_shukudai⟧⟦{出|だ}した→出す：01087_dasu⟧?
examples.english: By the way, did you turn in the homework?

examples.japanese: そういえば、⟦{来週|らいしゅう}→来週：00746_raishuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{会議|かいぎ}→会議：00710_kaigi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{場所|ばしょ}→場所：00829_basho⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{変|か}わった→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧⟦って→って：29146_tte⟧⟦{聞|き}いた→聞く：00483_kiku⟧⟦{気|き}→気：02199_ki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Come to think of it, I think I heard the location of next week's meeting has changed.

notes:
Literally 'if (one) says so' — そう (so/that way) + ⟦{言|い}えば→言う：00515_iu⟧ (if one says). Used when the current topic prompts the speaker to recall something related. The follow-up is usually loosely connected to what was just said.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- Sentence-initial only, followed by a comma.
- Often paired with ⟦けど→けど：09477_kedo⟧ or んだ⟦けど→けど：09477_kedo⟧ before stating the new point.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- そういえば、⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧…: come to think of it, in the old days …
- そういえば、⟦{聞|き}いた→聞く：00483_kiku⟧?: speaking of which, did you hear?
- そういえば、そうだ⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧: oh yeah, that's true (when reminded of something)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ところ→所：01137_tokoro⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧: by the way (deliberate topic change, not necessarily reminded by context)
- ⟦それはそうと→それはそうと：27572_sorehasouto⟧: by the way; that aside (more deliberate shift away from current topic)
- ちなみ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: incidentally; for your information (adds related info)
